title: What caused the Late Bronze Age collapse
summary: Competing theories for this collapse have been proposed since the 19th century, from drought to invasions and economic disruption. Most scholars now favour a combination of factors.
why: A whole world system of palaces, trade and writing fell within a few generations.

notes.problem: Source: 'It is likely that a combination of several factors is responsible' and names general systems collapse; record omitted both.

question: What brought down the interconnected Bronze Age kingdoms around 1200 BCE?
evidence: The collapse is dated to the late 13th to early 12th century BCE; proposed causes have been debated since the 19th century.
wouldSettle: Site-by-site dating of destructions compared with precise climate and conflict records.

theories.name: Climate change and drought
theories.idea: Drier conditions caused famine and weakened palace economies.

theories.name: Sea Peoples invasions
theories.idea: Raiders and migrants attacked coastal kingdoms.

theories.name: Economic and military change
theories.idea: Trade disruption, ironworking and new tactics undermined chariot-based palace states.

theories.name: Disease and volcanic eruptions
theories.idea: Epidemics or eruptions struck already stressed societies.
